name: simgaze
measures: Scenario 3 with the capture layer's simulated eye gaze instead of Quad Views' mouse simulation: every gaze consumer above the capture layer (Quad Views' focus, Cheeky's focus, Pupil shift, OFXR through Quad Views' focus layer) reads the same scripted gaze, with main-sequence saccades. rigtap.log: 'SIMULATED EYE GAZE ON', then 'ACTIVE ... served N (valid N ...)' once a second, N > 0 after the briefing. Quad Views log: 'Eye tracking is supported' even on a runtime that says it is not; 'DCSVR gaze: ... saccades' > 0. Capture around each jump: the focus field of view of the real frame after the jump moved by the commanded angle (+ lead). simgaze_trace.csv: what was served, for the verdict.
cannotJudge: The Pimax runtime's own foveated rendering and PVR eye API (not OpenXR); Cheeky's gaze when the runtime does not list XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction at all (its probe asks the loader, which may not report a layer's extension: check Cheeky's 'probe extension=' line); xrLocateSpaces (OpenXR 1.1) is not answered.
sideEffects: the real eye tracker is ignored for the whole flight (the layer answers every eye-gaze query); nothing outside the flown copy changes
PupilShift.ini in the flown copy gets [DepthBoost] PimaxPvrGaze=0 so that Depth boost reads the same gaze
90 submissions per capture = about 1 s at 90 Hz, so each window holds one or two jumps; scale 2 keeps it at 0.9 GB per capture
